token_notes.{{region_law}}: Renders as 'Rent Smart Wales licensed' in Wales or 'Redress scheme and client money protected' in England. It is the only legal proof phrase in any template; no template names Rent Smart Wales, the Renters' Rights Act or the Renting Homes Act unless the item carries a matching region field.
token_notes.{{rent_avg}}: The ONS average monthly rent for the area as a formatted figure, for example £650. Templates never compute a fee from it; the fee is always stated as 12% capped at £150.
token_notes.{{rent_change}}: The year-on-year change as a short phrase that reads after a figure, for example 'up 7.9%'.
token_notes.{{whatsapp_link}}: A wa.me link to the partner's number. Used at most once per Facebook post.
token_notes.{{area_url}}: The area page. The portal appends UTMs (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign=area-slug) at render time; templates carry none.

render_rules: British English, no exclamation marks, no emojis in flyers, letters, GBP or scripts; at most one emoji in a Facebook post (none are used here).

Region fields: 'england', 'wales' or 'both'. The portal renders only items whose region matches the area's region or is 'both'. Items with pillar 'london' render only for the London area (slug london), which covers every Greater London borough.
Letters and flyers carry no property-address token. Where a piece is addressed to one property, the portal's print step adds the address block above the greeting.
GBP description, services and posts must be re-measured after rendering: the limits below are checked on the template text, and long area names or partner names add characters.

Nothing here is legal advice. Dates and penalties are those verified in research/ENGLAND-REGIME-AND-AREAS.md and marketing/articles on 16 October 2026. Anything the research note marks [VERIFY] is either confirmed against a cited source before it appears in copy or left out of the copy; no [VERIFY] or [CONFIRM] tag sits in text a partner can render. Short-let copy talks about what we do: year-round demand, pricing by season, Flex Switch, the business-rates night test, council tax and the registers. It says nothing else about what a short let may or may not do, and makes no claim that short lets are unrestricted.

Flyers and letters are print pieces and use h1, h2 and h3 with the flyer-head class, plus p, ul, li and strong with flyer-body and flyer-foot. The print renderer passes that mark-up through unchanged; the p, ul, li, strong, a whitelist applies to area page content only.

Hello {{area}}. I'm {{partner}}; some of you will know me from around {{place_1}}. From this month I'm the Local Partner for Hello New Home, the letting agents, covering {{covers}}.

If you own a rental round here, two things worth knowing. The management fee is capped at £150 a month (12% up to that cap, no VAT), and there is no 12-month lock-in: 30 days' notice, no exit fee. If you're on a higher percentage with extras on top, it's worth ten minutes to compare.

I'm not going to fill the group with adverts. Head office in Swansea does the contracts, the deposits and the money; I do the viewings, inspections and check-ins here. Happy to answer any lettings question in the comments.

If you'd like a free, written rent review, the link is on our {{area}} page: {{area_url}}

fb_posts.title: What changed for landlords on 1 May 2026
fb_posts.text:
If you let a property in {{area}} and have not looked at the rules since last year, this is the short version of what changed on 1 May 2026.

Every tenancy is now periodic; fixed terms have gone. Tenants can leave on two months' notice. Section 21 no-fault notices have gone; possession runs through the Section 8 grounds. Rent can go up once a year, by notice, with two months' warning, and the tenant can challenge it at a tribunal. Before a new tenancy starts you must give a written statement of terms; the council can fine you up to £7,000 for missing it. The landlord database opens on 15 December 2026, region by region.

None of it is hard. It is dates and forms, and dates get missed around a day job. Hello New Home runs the calendar for every property it manages; I do the inspections here.

If you self-manage, download the free {{area}} Landlord Compliance Checklist from the area page. It is the list we use: {{area_url}}
fb_posts.image_hint: Calendar-style graphic with '1 May 2026' circled in pink and five short lines beneath: periodic tenancies, no Section 21, rent once a year, written statement, landlord database.

fb_posts.title: Five things English law expects from a landlord
fb_posts.text:
Five things the law now expects from you if you let a home in {{area}}, and what happens when one slips.

1. A written statement of terms before every new tenancy starts. Miss it and the council can fine you up to £7,000.
2. A Right to Rent check on every adult before they move in. Civil penalties apply per occupier and rise for a repeat.
3. The deposit protected within 30 days with the prescribed information, and never more than five weeks' rent.
4. Gas safety every year, an electrical report at least every five years, a smoke alarm on every storey, a carbon monoxide alarm wherever there is a fixed gas appliance.
5. A council licence where your council runs a scheme for your street or your property type.

Head office keeps all five on a calendar for every managed property; I do the inspections in {{area}}. Full Management is 12%, capped at £150 a month, no VAT.

Not ready to hand it over? The checklist is free on the area page: {{area_url}}

fb_posts.title: 3,198 penalties, almost all for the same two things
fb_posts.text:
Rent Smart Wales issued 3,198 fixed penalties in the year to May 2026, and almost all of them were for the same two things: not being registered as a landlord, and letting a property without a licence or a licensed agent.

Both have a simple fix. Registration is a form. The licence is a training course and an application, or you instruct a licensed agent and the agent requirement is met that way.

Hello New Home is a Rent Smart Wales licensed agent, so instructing us satisfies the agent licence for your {{area}} property, and the compliance calendar then keeps the renewal dates. If you want to stay self-managing, register and take the course; it is cheaper than the penalty.

Unsure which you need for your situation? Ask in the comments or use the free rent review on the area page and head office will tell you: {{area_url}}
fb_posts.image_hint: Plain text graphic, cream background: '3,198 fixed penalties. Two causes. Two fixes.' with the Rent Smart Wales logo omitted (not ours to use).

fb_posts.title: Mains-wired, interlinked, every storey
fb_posts.text:
Three fitness requirements that catch {{area}} landlords out under the Renting Homes (Wales) Act.

Smoke alarms: mains-powered, interlinked, on every storey. Battery alarms from the DIY shop do not meet the standard. Carbon monoxide: an alarm in every room with a gas, oil or solid-fuel appliance. Electrics: an electrical condition report at least every five years, with a copy to the contract-holder.

A home that fails these is treated as unfit for human habitation, and you cannot rely on a landlord's notice to end the contract while it is unfit. That is a big consequence for a £40 alarm.

Head office books the electrician and the alarm fit on the compliance calendar for every managed property, and I check them on the quarterly inspection. The free checklist on the area page lists all of the fitness points: {{area_url}}
fb_posts.image_hint: Close-up photo of a ceiling smoke alarm with the interlink light visible; overlay 'Mains. Interlinked. Every storey.'

fb_posts.title: Long let or short let in {{area}}?
fb_posts.text:
If you have a flat or a house in {{place_1}}, {{place_2}} or {{place_3}} you have probably wondered whether it would make more as a short let, or if it already is one, whether it is still worth it.

Nobody can tell you honestly unless they run both. A long let gives you one rent and one tenant. A short let can gross more, and then platform fees, cleaning, linen, utilities, empty weeks and management come off the top. Most people compare the headline numbers and get the decision wrong in one direction or the other.

Hello New Home does both, so head office will run a free SA Income Appraisal: your property as a long let versus a short let, net of everything, using {{area}} occupancy and nightly rates, plus a legality check for the address. Sometimes the answer is "stay as you are". Sometimes it is a few hundred pounds a month either way. If the long let wins, we say so.

I'm {{partner}}, the Local Partner for {{area}}. The appraisal form is on the area page: {{area_url}}

That is self-hosting. It is a second job that pays in reviews.

Full SA Management with Hello New Home covers dynamic pricing, guest vetting, 24/7 guest messaging, cleaning and linen coordination, restocking, maintenance, reviews, and a monthly owner statement with the night count built in. I'm here in {{area}} for changeovers and the things that need a person; head office handles the messages at 11.40pm. And because we manage long lets too, if the short-let numbers ever stop working we move you to a tenancy without re-onboarding.

fb_posts.title: London short stays book all year
fb_posts.text:
A short let in London is not a summer business. The guests are mostly working: staff and contractors at hospital trusts across the capital booking Sunday to Friday, contract staff in the City and at Canary Wharf, people relocating here who need a furnished flat for a month while they look, students between tenancies, and visitors who want to be a short train ride from the centre.

That is why we price by season and by day of the week rather than from a national average, and why a property with us can move between short stays, furnished lets of a month or more and a tenancy with the same agent and no re-onboarding.

It is also why the honest answer is sometimes the tenancy. Hello New Home runs both, so the free appraisal shows your flat as a long let and as a short let, net of platform fees, cleaning, utilities, empty nights and management, with your borough's licensing position alongside. If the tenancy wins, we say so.

fb_posts.text:
People message me most weeks looking for a home around {{place_1}}, {{place_2}} and {{place_3}}, and the honest answer is that good ones go before they reach the portals.

Two things that help. Register your search with us (area, bedrooms, move date, pets if any) and head office will call you when something fits rather than you refreshing Rightmove. And have your references ready: ID, proof of income and your last landlord's details, so a viewing can become an application the same day.

If you are a landlord in those areas with a home coming empty, the same post applies to you in reverse: Tenant Find is £495, no let no fee, and Full Management is 12% capped at £150 a month.

The ONS figure for {{area}} this month: average rent {{rent_avg}}, {{rent_change}} on a year ago.

Two things to do with it. If you are a landlord who has not reviewed the rent in a while, it is a prompt, not a target; the right figure for your property depends on the street, the condition and the season, and a rent you cannot let at is worth nothing. If you are renting, it is a check on what you are being asked for.

We give both sides the same figure. The landlord's free rent review and the figure we market at are the same number, which is why landlords sometimes hear "lower than you hoped" from us. Honest beats empty.

fb_posts.title: What a quarterly inspection actually involves
fb_posts.text:
A quarterly inspection in {{area}} takes me about 40 minutes and produces 30 to 50 photos. Here is what I am looking at.

Damp and ventilation: the corners of the bathroom and the back of the wardrobes, not the hallway. Alarms: pressed, not glanced at. The boiler pressure and the date on the gas certificate. Anything the tenant mentions in passing, because a dripping tap now is a ceiling later. Then a short written report to the landlord with the photos and any work that needs booking, which head office then books.

It is not about catching anyone out. Most of what I find is a landlord's problem waiting to be small rather than large.

Inspections are included in Full Management, 12% capped at £150 a month. Rent review on the area page if you want to see the fee on your own property: {{area_url}}
fb_posts.image_hint: Photo of the partner's hand holding a phone camera up to a bathroom ceiling corner, or a clipboard with the inspection checklist; no tenant possessions identifiable.

fb_posts.title: The most boring spreadsheet we own
fb_posts.text:
Every managed property in {{area}} has a row on head office's compliance calendar: gas safety date, electrical report date, EPC expiry, alarm test, deposit protection date, licence renewal where the council runs a scheme, and the written agreement date.

Each one gets booked a month before it is due. The landlord gets a message when it is done and a copy of the certificate. That is the whole system, and it is the reason the letters other landlords get about fines do not arrive.

It is also why the fee is a flat 12% capped at £150 a month with nothing added: the work is the same every month whether the rent is {{rent_avg}} or more.

If you self-manage and would like the same calendar as a one-page checklist, it is free on the area page: {{area_url}}

Hello New Home is taking on a small founding group of Local Partners in towns across England and Wales, and I'm one of them here in {{area}}, so here is what it actually is.

No buy-in. You bring the landlords and short-let owners in your patch; head office in Swansea does everything regulated: contracts, deposits, client money, compliance, rent collection, the repairs desk. Introducers earn 25% of the net management fee on every instruction they bring, for as long as it is managed, plus £100 per short-let unit live. Area Partners, once they have proven it, take a postcode territory and earn 50% on their own instructions, with a £99 a month systems fee from month four. The first three months are a proving period and either side can walk.

It is not a franchise and it is not a course. It is a brand, a back office and a territory, and the local hustle is yours. Worked examples are illustrative, never typical.

If you know your town and are already in property in some way, the programme page is here: https://hellonewhome.co.uk/partners-programme

posts.title: What changed on 1 May 2026
posts.text:
Since 1 May 2026 every new tenancy in England needs a written statement of terms before it starts, rent can rise once a year by notice, no-fault notices have gone, and the landlord database opens on 15 December 2026. None of it is hard. It is dates and forms, and dates get missed around a day job.

Full Management includes all of it, 12% capped at £150 a month, with {{partner_first}} doing the inspections in {{area}}. A council licence may also apply to your street or property type; we check before we market.

Self-managing? The free {{area}} Landlord Compliance Checklist is the list we use.

posts.title: The five dates every Welsh landlord has to keep
posts.text:
Rent Smart Wales registration and licence. The written statement within 14 days of the occupation date. Mains-powered, linked smoke alarms on every floor and a carbon monoxide alarm in any room with a gas, oil or solid-fuel appliance. An electrical inspection at least every five years. The deposit protected within 30 days.

Miss the written statement and you can't serve a landlord's notice until six months after you finally hand it over. Miss Rent Smart Wales and a tribunal can order rent to be repaid.

We've put the full list on one page, free. It's the same list we run as a calendar for every property we manage in {{area}}; {{partner_first}} checks the alarms on every inspection.

PS. If the property let privately and you are now managing it yourself, the free {{area}} Landlord Compliance Checklist on the area page has the dates you now have to keep. No strings.

If you would rather not hear from us about this property again, reply "no thanks" to the WhatsApp number or email lettings@hellonewhome.co.uk and we will remove the address from our list.

scripts.title: Cold call to a landlord (TPS-screened list only)
scripts.text:
Open: "Hi, is that [name]? It's {{partner_first}} from Hello New Home, the letting agents. I'm the Local Partner for {{area}}. Have I caught you at a bad time, or have you got two minutes?"

If bad time: "No problem. When's better, this evening or tomorrow lunchtime?" Book it. Hang up.

If "what's it about?": "Two things, quickly. We're the agent with the capped management fee: 12%, but never more than £150 a month, no VAT, and no 12-month lock-in. And I'm calling landlords in {{area}} to offer a free rent review: an honest figure for what your place should be letting at this month, no obligation. Is your property on [street] still let out?"

Discover, then be quiet: "How are you managing it at the moment, yourself or through an agent?" If self-managing: "What's the bit you'd most like off your plate?" If with an agent: "What are they charging you all-in, if you don't mind me asking, and when does the agreement run to?" "Is it just the one, or do you have others?"

Position, matching what they said, not everything: arrears, "rent collection and arrears chasing sit with head office, and there's a rent guarantee option for £25 a month on top if you want the worry gone"; fee creep, "the cap is the point: on the {{area}} average of {{rent_avg}} you'd pay 12% of that and never more than £150, with no renewal or inspection fees"; lock-in, "30 days' notice, any time, no exit fee"; compliance, "gas, electrics, EPC, alarms, licence renewals, the agreement paperwork, all on a calendar head office runs, and I do the inspections here."

Ask: "Shall I book you in for the free rent review? Head office will call within one working day, it takes about ten minutes, and you'll have a written figure by email. If the numbers don't stack up, you've lost ten minutes."

Close: "Best number and email? And the address? Any time you'd rather not be called? Thanks [name], you'll hear from head office by [day]. This is my direct number, {{whatsapp_display}}, if anything comes up."

If no: "Understood. Can I pop a one-page fee sheet in the post for when the renewal comes round?" Log the outcome and the renewal date. If "take me off your list": "Of course, I'll do that now. Sorry to have bothered you." Log the opt-out the same hour.
scripts.notes: Never name another agent, never guess their fees, never say guaranteed. {{region_law}} is the proof line if asked who regulates us.

scripts.title: Doorstep, board-canvass streets
scripts.text:
Use on streets where you have logged boards. Never after 7pm, never where a "no cold callers" sticker is displayed.

Homeowner answers: "Hi, sorry to knock. I'm {{partner_first}}, the Local Partner for Hello New Home, the letting agents, and I'm working this street this month. You'll have seen the boards at number [x] and number [y]. Two quick questions and then I'll leave you alone: do you own any rental property yourself, and do you know who owns number [x]?"

If they own a rental: "Rather than keep you on the doorstep, can I get head office to call you for a free rent review? Ten minutes, written figure, no obligation. The fee's 12% capped at £150 a month and there's no lock-in, so there's nothing to sign today."

If they know the owner: "Would you mind passing on my card? I won't ask you for their number. If they'd like a free rent review the details are on there." Hand over a card. Thank them. Leave.

If neither: "Thanks very much, that's all I needed. Have a good day."

Tenant answers at a board property: "Hi, sorry to disturb you. I'm {{partner_first}} from Hello New Home, the letting agents. I'm not here about your tenancy and I'm not going to ask you anything about your landlord. Could I leave a card for the owner in case they're ever reviewing who manages the place? Thanks, that's all." Do not ask the tenant about the rent, the landlord or whether they are happy.

No answer: the "sorry we missed you" card through the door, dated and initialled.
scripts.notes: Cards carry {{area_url}}, {{whatsapp_display}} and {{phone}}. Log every board, every card and every opt-out the same day.

scripts.title: Networking intro, 20 seconds and the round-the-room version
scripts.text:
Twenty seconds: "I'm {{partner_first}}, Local Partner for Hello New Home, the letting agents with the capped management fee: 12%, never more than £150 a month, no VAT, and no lock-in. We do long lets, shared houses and short lets, so a landlord can switch between them without changing agent. I cover {{covers}}. If you know anyone round here who's fed up with their agent, or running an Airbnb and wondering if it's worth it, I'll get them a free rent review or a free short-let appraisal from head office. Who do you know?"

Round-the-room: "{{partner_first}}, Hello New Home, capped-fee lettings and short-let management for {{area}}. I'm looking for landlords who are fed up with fees and short-let owners who are fed up full stop."

If asked "so you're the agent?": "No. Hello New Home is: {{region_law}}, insured, and that's who the agreement and the money sit with. I'm the person who turns up in {{area}}."
scripts.notes: One ask per conversation. Take a card, don't just give one, and send the WhatsApp first message within 24 hours.

scripts.title: WhatsApp first message (replies and follow-ups only, never cold)
scripts.text:
After a networking meeting or a card: "Hi [name], it's {{partner_first}} from Hello New Home, we met at [event] on [day]. As promised, the short version: Full Management is 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month, no VAT, 30 days' notice to leave. Tenant Find is £495, no let no fee. The full fee sheet is here: {{area_url}}. If you'd like the free rent review, send me the address and head office will call within one working day. No pressure either way, and good to meet you."

Reply to someone who posted "can anyone recommend a letting agent?": "Hi [name], saw your post in [group]. I'm the Local Partner for Hello New Home in {{area}}, so I'm biased, but here's the straight version: 12% capped at £150 a month, no lock-in, {{region_law}}, head office in Swansea, me on the ground here. If it's useful, head office will do a free written rent review so you've got a number to compare any agent against. Want me to set that up? If not, no problem, and good luck with the let."

Reply to someone who posted about a problem (arrears, a bad agent, a council letter): "Hi [name], sorry you're dealing with that. I'm with Hello New Home (Local Partner for {{area}}). I can't advise on your specific situation, but I can get someone at head office who deals with [arrears / licensing / notices] every day to give you a ten-minute call, no charge and no pressure to move to us. Would that help? If you'd rather just have the number for the council's housing team or Shelter, say so and I'll send it."

Reply to someone who messaged first about fees: "Thanks for getting in touch, [name]. Everything's on the fee sheet so there are no surprises: Full Management 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month; setup £295, waived if you're moving an existing tenancy over; Tenant Find £495, no let no fee; rent guarantee is Full Management plus £25 a month. 30 days' notice to leave, any time. Full list: {{area_url}}. The quickest next step is the free rent review; head office calls within a working day. Shall I book it, and what's the address?"
scripts.notes: Send the link as a second message so it previews. Never message an individual who hasn't posted, messaged or met you first.

scripts.title: Review ask (after a win, once, everyone)
scripts.text:
When: the day a tenant moves in and the first rent clears; the day a repair is closed; the first monthly statement after a switch; the first owner statement on a short let. Ask once; one reminder after seven days; then stop.

Landlord, by WhatsApp or text: "Hi [name], it's {{partner_first}} at Hello New Home. First rent on [street] has cleared and [tenant first name] is in. If the last few weeks went the way you'd want, would you leave us a line on Google? [link]. If anything didn't, reply here and I'll sort it first."

Tenant, seven days in: "Hi [name], it's {{partner_first}} at Hello New Home. A week in at [street]. Agreement, deposit certificate and alarms all as they should be? If yes, we'd be grateful for a Google review: [link]. If anything's not right, reply here and we'll fix it."

In person, at the end of a check-in or a closed repair: "One small ask. If this went well, a sentence on Google helps the next landlord or tenant in {{area}} choose. I'll text you the link. If it didn't go well, tell me now and I'd rather fix it than read about it."

Rules: ask everyone who reaches the trigger, not just the happy ones; never offer money, discounts or fee waivers; never ask for a star rating or particular words; never ask while standing over them; head office replies to every review within two working days.
scripts.notes: The review link is the area profile's Google review short link; HQ sends it to the partner on day one.

scripts.title: Referral ask (landlords and short-let owners, after the first good month)
scripts.text:
When: after the first statement that lands the way you said it would, or a repair handled well. Not at signing.

By WhatsApp or in person: "Glad the first month went the way we said. Can I ask one thing? Most of our landlords in {{area}} come from other landlords. If you know anyone round {{place_1}}, {{place_2}} or {{place_3}} who's paying a percentage plus extras, or self-managing and getting the letters, would you pass my number on, {{whatsapp_display}}? I won't contact them unless they contact me. The fee sheet is the same for them as it was for you, and the rent review is free."

If they ask what's in it for them: "Nothing beyond the same service you're getting. We don't pay for introductions and we don't want to be the agent who does. If a friend of yours ends up with a capped fee and no lock-in, that's the return."

If they say yes: "Thank you. Easiest is to forward them this message: 'This is {{partner_first}} at Hello New Home, Local Partner for {{area}}. 12% capped at £150 a month, no lock-in, free rent review in a working day: {{area_url}}.' That's all they need."

Mentees and people in property who might want more than a referral: "If you'd rather earn from it, there's an Introducer route: 25% of the net management fee on every instruction you bring, for as long as it's managed. No buy-in. Ask me and I'll send the programme page, hellonewhome.co.uk/partners-programme."
scripts.notes: Introducer mention only to people already in the mentoring orbit or in property. Never offer a landlord a payment for a referral.
